applied.old: Stop immediately if it causes flatness, anhedonia, apathy, emotional blunting, new depression, agitation, irritability, insomnia, dizziness, palpitations, nausea, loose stools, diarrhea, or increased craving. Only the stomach problems showed up in the human trials, but the flatness happens in practice, so do not "push through" numbness. If agmatine makes the world more gray, it is the wrong tool for that phase.
applied.new: Agmatine can leave some folks flat and numb, according to reports online (although in the human studies we've only seen stomach problems), so stop it right away if you notice you're flatter or more depressed than before you started. I wouldn't push through that signal, because a few people say the numbness hung on for weeks after they quit, so it's not like one of those side effects that you'd only feel at first. Also stop if agmatine winds you up instead (more irritable, can't sleep), or you get dizziness, palpitations, nausea, loose stools or stronger cravings.

applied.inserted: For the zinc, I'd use zinc carnosine, up to 75 mg daily (16 mg elemental zinc), which is a standard dose. This form also helps repair leaky gut ([Mahmood, et al, 2007](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1856764)), and it's better tolerated than other forms of zinc, but if it causes nausea, take less at a time. Zinc should be taken with copper (1–2 mg elemental; avoid cupric oxide, and use copper gluconate or citrate). For L-serine, I'd do 5–15 g, depending how it feels. Up to 30 g has been used in trials for neurodegenerative conditions ([Levine, et al, 2017](https://doi.org/10.1080/21678421.2016.1221971)), but with more GI distress at higher doses.

revised_58.new: For the zinc, I'd use zinc carnosine, since it's better tolerated than other forms of zinc and also helps repair leaky gut ([Mahmood, et al, 2007](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1856764)). A standard dose is up to 75 mg a day, which holds 16 mg of elemental zinc, and if it causes nausea, take less at a time. Zinc can lower your copper over time, so I'd also take 1–2 mg of elemental copper a day, as copper gluconate or citrate (not cupric oxide, which is poorly absorbed). For L-serine, I'd do 5–15 g a day, depending how it feels. Higher doses bring more GI distress, though up to 30 g a day has been used in trials for neurodegenerative conditions ([Levine, et al, 2017](https://doi.org/10.1080/21678421.2016.1221971)).
